title: AI Daily Briefing
description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, open and local models, and AI in defense.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 20–23. New: OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available on GPT-6 Luna; Google Cloud previewed Agent Compute Engine; and an Anthropic-managed Claude deployment on Google Cloud reached general availability on Oct. 23. NVIDIA's Minerva operations platform is on the data center page. No new Anthropic model card and no new OpenAI model release were found. The Oct. 20 toxin-binder note and the Orchestra Bio acquisition were outside this brief and were removed.

items.headline: Anthropic adds physicist Christopher Stubbs to the Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said Oct. 21 that Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist and former dean of science at Harvard, has joined its Long-Term Benefit Trust. Anthropic says the Trust can appoint a majority of the board and that trustees advise leadership on decisions involving AI risks and societal impacts. Stubbs, whom Anthropic calls the Trust's first physicist, joins chair Neil Buddy Shah, Richard Fontaine, and former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke. Anthropic also said it published its first Public Benefit Report this week, and that the trustees helped define the five charter pillars the report measures.

items.headline: OpenAI makes the Decisions API generally available on GPT-6 Luna
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 22 that the Decisions API is generally available. It uses GPT-6 Luna for questions with bounded answers, and OpenAI says it is up to 10 times faster than calling GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. Since the public beta, OpenAI has added a native GPT-Live integration, prompt caching, inference residency in the United States and the European Union, native JSON inputs, images in the instructions, and a limit of 400 questions per request, twice the previous limit. OpenAI says input costs $0.10 per million tokens, cached input costs $0.01 per million tokens, and there is no charge for output tokens.

items.headline: OpenAI models and Codex are coming to Google Cloud Model Garden
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 21 it is partnering with Google Cloud to put frontier models and Codex agent workflows in Model Garden. Customers will be able to buy the models through Google Cloud Marketplace and draw down Google Cloud commit. OpenAI also said the models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent. General availability is planned in the coming weeks. Microsoft remains OpenAI's primary cloud partner. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian framed it as model choice for a given job.

items.headline: Google Cloud makes an Anthropic-managed Claude deployment generally available
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 23 that an Anthropic-managed option for Claude models on Google Cloud is generally available, alongside the existing Google-managed option. Google says both deliver the same frontier models on day zero, the same pricing, and Google Cloud billing, including drawdown of eligible commitments. On the Anthropic-managed option, Anthropic is the data processor under its own terms, and Claude platform features such as Managed Agents in beta, skills, and code execution are available on day zero. Google names Claude Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 5.5, and says customers authenticate with Google Cloud IAM.

items.headline: Google Cloud previews Agent Compute Engine, one hardware-isolated microVM per agent
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 22 at AGNTCon and MCPCon that Agent Compute Engine, which already runs Gemini as an agent for work tasks, will be available in preview in the coming months. Google says each agent gets a hardware-isolated microVM with its own guest kernel, short-lived credentials, and a Hyperdisk, and that an idle microVM can be paused and restored from a snapshot. For Kubernetes, Google introduced open-source Agent Substrate and said a benchmark of 200,000 agents sustained 500 activations per second with suspend and resume under 500 milliseconds. Google also said it is extending Gemini agent governance, including Agent Gateway, to more runtimes.

items.headline: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch stack for TPUs
items.summary: At PyTorch Conference on Oct. 20, Google said TorchTPU, its native PyTorch stack for Cloud TPUs, is open source on GitHub. Google says TPUs can now be used as a native PyTorch target alongside GPUs and CPUs, with the tools teams already use, including vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, TorchTitan, Ray, Hugging Face and LiteRT. The PyTorch project published its own introduction the same day. This is a software-portability move: the same model code has a path onto TPU hardware without a separate stack.

items.headline: Google Cloud's A5X instances put Vera Rubin NVL72 in bare metal; GA is next month
items.summary: Google Cloud told GTC Berlin on Oct. 21 that new A5X bare-metal instances use the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. General availability is coming next month, with new regions aimed at EMEA data residency. Virgo Network is the scale-out fabric: Google says a single site can grow to 80,000 Rubin GPUs and multi-site deployments to 960,000. A5X will also support Managed Lustre with GPUDirect Storage and GKE scheduling features. Ineffable Intelligence was named as an early customer in NVIDIA's parallel write-up.

items.headline: NVIDIA expands Isaac at GTC Berlin with a reference humanoid and Isaac Lab 3.0
items.summary: NVIDIA announced Oct. 21 an expansion of the Isaac robotics platform: a reference humanoid, new datasets and runtime, and updates to the robot-learning framework. Agile Robots' Agile ONE SN is a humanoid reference built on Isaac GR00T and Jetson Thor, with planned integration of the Halos safety stack. Isaac adds an Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0, and open reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with Isaac and Cosmos on DGX Station. NVIDIA named European robotics firms, including ABB, KUKA, NEURA and Universal Robots, as building on the stack.

items.headline: NVIDIA shows the local stack in Berlin: RTX Spark, DGX Spark and DGX Station
items.summary: NVIDIA's GTC Berlin blog says the company is showing its local AI hardware lineup. RTX Spark, which launched the prior week, runs personal agents on Windows PCs. DGX Spark is for developers on Linux. DGX Station is for enterprise teams on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December. Underdog Desktop Agent was announced as available for RTX Spark. This is the on-prem and deskside path, separate from the Vera Rubin cloud instances.

items.headline: OpenAI says partners that host its models must meet its safeguards; new usage rules start Nov. 20
items.summary: OpenAI said Oct. 21 it has written policies so safeguards stay consistent whether people use its models directly, through a hosting partner, or through a reseller. Those policies require partners to investigate possible violations and to coordinate enforcement. Updated Usage Policies take effect Nov. 20, 2026, and require services that provide direct access, such as model routers or AI gateways, to get OpenAI's review and approval first. OpenAI also said it is working with customers on SafetyIDs, which a customer can provide so OpenAI can tell end users apart in an investigation without learning who they are.

items.headline: Project Agincourt's roadmap measures autonomy by how fast a fielded fix reaches the fight
items.summary: The Department of War said Oct. 21 that Owen West and Senior Chief Max Strasiser sent the joint force and industry an operational roadmap for the Autonomous Warfare Command. The release says the model pushes procurement decisions and dollars to frontline warfighters, and that urgency does not excuse imprecision. Success, they said, is how fast an operational problem gets a fielded solution that can scale, not a paperwork milestone. The release does not name a new contract vehicle or a prime.
